scope: core program agent_auth (root crate), unaudited devnet prototype

tests.ignored_detail: 6 devnet.rs (live network, not run), 1 layout.rs, 1 layout_v1.rs (golden-fixture writer)
tests.non_vacuity: AGENT_AUTH_ALLOW_SKIP unset. Every early 'return' in tests is a let-else on a setup that panics when the .so is missing; confirmed by running regression_cu with AGENT_AUTH_SO=/nonexistent.so, which panics 'program binary not found'.

mutation.method: Hand-written source mutants of src/ (guard deletions, comparison flips, error-variant swaps, dropped state writes, off-by-one and 31-of-32-byte key compares, constants/layout changes), applied one at a time to a pristine copy, built with cargo build-sbf and run against the full test suite with AGENT_AUTH_ALLOW_SKIP unset. A control run (unmutated source) passed and its .so was byte-identical to the baseline build.
mutation.real_gaps_closed: All four were closed with targeted tests (tests/mutation_survivors.rs, tests/error_matrix.rs, tests/state_unit.rs). Each new test was verified to fail on its own mutant and pass on the real source, in a private clone. The full mutant sweep was NOT re-run after the last tests were added.
equivalent_mutants: S18: swap_remove_permission `if idx != last` -> `if true` (self-copy no-op)
V06: revoke `account_data.fill(0)` removed (close() zeroes the data length)
V08: revoke `*mandate_lamports = 0` removed (close() zeroes lamports right after)
mutation.caveat: V06 and V08 rely on pinocchio 0.9.3 close() semantics. Mutation score is a statement about the tests' sensitivity to these mutants, not about the absence of bugs.

rows.note: re-measured on the final tree (the gate run recorded 6118 before the later source state; docs/BENCHMARKS.md section 1.1)

program_size_note: target/deploy/agent_auth.so from this gate's build; the core-fix report quoted 36488, the 16-byte difference is from a later source state. Baseline v0.1 was 29608.
